questions.context: In a kitchen in Medellín, a mother shows eggs, cheese, milk and corn flour for arepas.

options.feedback: Chair and table are furniture, only spoon is a tool.
Eggs, cheese and milk are common cooking ingredients.
Shirt, pants and socks are clothes, not ingredients.
Car, bus and bike are transport, not ingredients.

questions.explanation: Esta pregunta presenta vocabulario básico de ingredientes en inglés. También conecta las palabras con la preparación de arepas colombianas.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: What are "cut", "mix" and "eat" in a recipe?
questions.context: In Bogotá, a recipe says: "Cut the tomatoes. Mix the salad. Eat with your family."

options.feedback: These words are actions, not names of fruits.
These words describe cooking actions, not animals.
Cut, mix and eat tell the reader what action to do.
These words are verbs, not colors of food.

questions.explanation: Los verbos de acción son la base de las recetas en inglés. También se comprende que los imperativos indican qué hacer paso a paso.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Choose the correct imperative to complete the instruction.
questions.context: In Cali, a boy helps his grandmother: "_____ the cheese for the arepas, please."

options.feedback: "He grates" describes a person and is not an imperative order.
"Grate" is the base verb used for polite imperative instructions.
"Grated" is past tense and is not used for instructions.
"Grating" is the -ing form and is not an imperative.

questions.explanation: El imperativo usa el verbo en forma base sin sujeto. También se practica con verbos de cocina como grate en recetas familiares.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: What is the correct order to make arepas?
questions.context: In Cartagena, students read an arepa recipe: "First, mix corn flour and water. Then, add cheese. Finally, cook on a hot pan."

options.feedback: Cooking is the last step, not the first step.
Mixing flour and water comes first in the recipe.

options.text: Mix flour and water, add cheese, cook on the pan.
options.feedback: This order follows first, then and finally in the recipe.
Eating is after cooking, not part of the preparation order.

questions.explanation: Leer recetas exige seguir conectores como first, then y finally. También se aplica la secuencia correcta para preparar arepas colombianas.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which verb means to cook in hot oil?
questions.context: At home in Bucaramanga, a girl cooks: "Boil the water for the soup. Fry the egg. Bake the bread."

options.feedback: To boil means to cook in hot bubbling water.
To fry means to cook food in hot oil in a pan.
To bake means to cook in the oven with dry heat.
To wash means to clean with water, not to cook.

questions.explanation: Los verbos boil, fry y bake describen formas distintas de cocinar. También se amplía el vocabulario culinario con acciones visibles en casa.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: What can you conclude about these arepas?
questions.context: In Pereira, a recipe says: "You need 2 cups of corn flour, 1 cup of cheese and a little salt. Do not add sugar."

options.text: They are sweet because they have sugar.
options.feedback: The recipe says do not add sugar, so they are not sweet.

options.text: They have cheese and salt but no sugar.
options.feedback: The ingredient list includes cheese and salt and excludes sugar.

options.text: They need no corn flour or cheese.
options.feedback: The recipe asks for 2 cups of flour and 1 cup of cheese.

options.text: They are made only with water.
options.feedback: The recipe lists flour, cheese and salt, not only water.

questions.explanation: Analizar ingredientes permite distinguir lo que lleva y lo que no lleva una receta. También se trabaja la lectura detallada de cantidades en inglés.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.context: In Santa Marta, a teacher compares: "She mixes the juice" and "Mix the juice."

options.text: The first describes a person, the second gives an instruction.
options.feedback: "She mixes" describes an action and "Mix" orders the action.
Only the second sentence without subject is an imperative.
Both sentences are in the present, not in the past.

options.text: The first is an instruction, the second describes a person.
options.feedback: The roles are reversed; the imperative has no subject.

questions.explanation: El imperativo omite el sujeto y usa el verbo base para ordenar. También se contrasta con el presente simple que sí incluye sujeto.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which recipe is the best for a fifth grader?
questions.context: In Manizales, two recipes for fruit salad appear: one lists steps clearly, the other has no order and unsafe steps.

options.text: Cut quickly without help, run with the knife, taste nothing.
options.feedback: These steps are unsafe and have no clear cooking order.

options.text: Mix everything dirty, never wash fruits, eat unwashed food.
options.feedback: Not washing fruits is unhealthy and the steps are unclear.

options.text: Wash the fruits, cut carefully with an adult, mix and serve.
options.feedback: These steps are safe, ordered and easy for a child with help.

options.text: Burn the fruits, add soap, serve cold stones.
options.feedback: These steps are dangerous and use things that are not food.

questions.explanation: Evaluar recetas implica revisar orden, claridad y seguridad. También se promueve cocinar con un adulto y lavar bien las frutas colombianas.
questions.subject: ingles
